---
title: "Assignment 3 — Geometry optimization and equation of state"
---

Laboratory 3 starts from the MgO model used in the previous activity and asks
two new questions:

> **What is the equilibrium geometry predicted by our computational model?**

and

> **How does the energy of that crystal change when we compress or expand it?**

The work is divided into two connected parts:

1. a full geometry optimization of MgO;
2. a static energy–volume equation-of-state calculation.

The optimized structure from the first part becomes the reference structure for
the second.

## Before the laboratory

Read:

- **Laboratory 3 — From equilibrium structure to an equation of state**;
- the updated **CRYSTAL input and output field guide**;
- the **CluMiner** quick reference if you need to review job submission.

Then update your personal workspace:

```bash
update-course
```

and create the Laboratory 3 working directory:

```bash
start-lab 03
```

Open:

```text
work/lab03/
```

You should find:

```text
01-geometry-optimization.ipynb
02-equation-of-state.ipynb
inputs/
outputs/
reference-results/
```

## Use the k-point sampling you selected in Laboratory 2

The geometry and EOS calculations should use the SHRINK value justified by your
Laboratory 2 convergence test.

The distributed inputs do not select a SHRINK value for you. They contain the
placeholder `<X> <X>`, which you must replace with the value that you selected
and justified in Laboratory 2. Keep that value fixed throughout Laboratory 3.

## Cluster resources

Use the same resource request as before:

```bash
cluminer-crystal INPUT.d12 --cores-per-node 2 --threads 2
```

Do not increase the number of cores.

## What you will produce

At the end of the activity your notebook should contain:

- the optimized MgO lattice parameter and cell volume;
- a comparison between the experimental starting geometry and the static DFT
  equilibrium geometry;
- an explanation of why the Mg and O fractional coordinates do not move;
- an energy–volume dataset around the optimized structure;
- a third-order Birch–Murnaghan (BM3) fit;
- the fitted $V_0$, $K_0$ and $K'_0$;
- an $E(V)$ plot;
- a $P(V)$ plot reconstructed from the fitted energy relation;
- a short interpretation of the bulk modulus.

The repeated extraction and fitting steps are handled by Quantas so that the
scientific work remains focused on interpretation rather than transcription.
